name: excitement
quote: The kids at the party were running around happily.
description: A heightened state of energy in response to participating in or considering a positive or negative experience.
perceptions: Something is happening or is going to happen.
It's going to be very positive or very negative.
My energy level is high enough to be able to properly participate in the event.
results: A state of physiological arousal – increased heart rate, adrenaline, heightened awareness.

guidance.description: Emotions are contagious. An excited, high-energy state, whether enthusiasm or anger, has a pull on everyone in the area. It may be helpful to understand this so you can affect others positively and resist being pulled in directions you're not comfortable with.

examples: She was excited to go to the amusement park.
The speaker stirred the crowd into a frenzy with his provocative statements.

commentaries.quote: In English, 'excitement' usually refers to something positive, but it can be used more generally to mean a vigorous response. For example, someone who's really angry could be considered 'excited'.

Among a great many other things that chess teaches you is to control the initial excitement you feel when you see something that looks good. It trains you to think before grabbing and to think just as objectively when you're in trouble.
In motivating people, you've got to engage their minds and their hearts. I motivate people, I hope, by example - and perhaps by excitement, by having productive ideas to make others feel involved.
Character is the ability to carry out a good resolution long after the excitement of the moment has passed.
